# 643: Specializing in the Element of Surprise (Two-in-One Chapter)

An open battle field between Laverre City and the Poké Ball factory.

One good thing about the Pokémon world was that battle venues were extremely common. As long as you wanted to battle, you could find suitable battle locations almost anywhere.

If worst came to worst, the wilderness would work too.

And Drasna was obviously "premeditated"—she had already scouted out the battle location.

In a secluded, empty battle field.

Johan and Drasna stood on opposite sides of the battle arena, each holding Poké Balls, ready for battle.

Originally, Johan had wanted a simple 1v1 format. After all, this was just an ordinary sparring match, and with no audience, winning or losing didn't matter at all.

But Drasna expressed wanting to have a 3v3 rotation battle with Johan.

Compared to 1v1, 3v3 indeed tested a trainer's abilities more, while also significantly reducing the luck factor.

And Johan just wanted to say, luck?

Hah—

What's that? Utterly dismissive.

"Ready?" Drasna opened her eyes, her expression somewhat serious.

"Of course."

Johan immediately threw the Poké Ball in his hand without hesitation. At the same time, Drasna on the opposite side also threw her Poké Ball.

Two flashes of red light.

"Yoji!"

Appearing before Johan was the solid Larvitar, which hit the ground with a dull thud, raising a thin layer of dust.

The first Pokémon Drasna summoned was Dragalge!

It looked like a seahorse with purple skin, surrounded by what appeared to be withered seaweed, with only the red leaves on its head looking somewhat vibrant.

"Dragalge, evolution of Skrelp, Poison and Dragon-type Mock Kelp Pokémon. It has a violent temperament and is extremely territorial. It's a highly toxic Pokémon—dangerous! Dangerous! Rotom!"

Rotom's screen flashed with red lights representing danger.

Dragalge?

Johan raised an eyebrow slightly.

As everyone knew, Fairy-type was extremely effective against Dragon-type, not only dealing double damage to Dragon-types but also being immune to Dragon-type attacks.

And Poison-type was the reverse—it was effective against Fairy-type.

So although it was a Dragon-type Pokémon, Dragalge actually wasn't afraid of Fairy-types; instead, it countered them.

Obviously.

As the "Dragon-type Elite Four of the Fairy Pokémon Origin Region," Drasna had ways to deal with Fairy-types.

However...

Johan hadn't sent out a Fairy-type Pokémon.

"Larvitar?"

Seeing Larvitar, Drasna's reaction was even stronger than Johan's reaction to seeing Dragalge.

She squinted slightly, glancing at Johan.

In at least an Elite Four-level battle, sending out an unevolved pseudo-legendary cub.

Either Johan completely didn't take this battle seriously, or... this Larvitar was extraordinary!

In Drasna's view, it must be the latter.

However...

Strategically despise the enemy, tactically respect the enemy.

So.

Drasna's lips curved slightly. "What a cute little one."

"Yoji! Yoji!"

Sure enough, after hearing Drasna's words, Larvitar got agitated, clenching its small fists and gesturing twice at Drasna and Dragalge.

Where's the cute part! Haven't you seen these fists as big as sandbags!

Johan lightly held his forehead.

Aunt Drasna really was...

But using psychological warfare against a Pokémon Psychology expert's Pokémon—wasn't that a bit too dismissive of Johan's presence?

Strike first!

"Larvitar, Sandstorm!"

"Yoji!"

Larvitar, which had been making a fuss the previous second, immediately dropped its expression upon hearing Johan's command and stomped heavily on the ground.

Bang!!

The ground seemed to tremble slightly, raising a cloud of dust while sand began to fly.

Seeing this, Drasna was somewhat surprised.

She hadn't expected... this little one, despite seeming rash, was quite clever.

Moreover, judging from this Sandstorm, this Larvitar was indeed as she'd guessed—not weak.

Swish swish swish—

Sand filled the air. In just an instant, dust covered the entire field, each grain of sand scraping against Dragalge's body like a small knife, bringing tiny stings of pain.

"Dragalge, move around, Aqua Tail!" Drasna said in a low voice.

Splash splash—

Following Drasna's command, Dragalge immediately moved. Water surged from its body, gathering at its tail.

The water current carried Dragalge, somewhat compensating for its naturally slow movement speed.

Moreover, the appearance of water flow also somewhat alleviated the stinging sensation brought by the sandstorm.

Dragalge began circling around Larvitar, water splashes and wet marks leaving circles on the ground.

"Now!"

Splash—

The accumulated Aqua Tail struck decisively after finding an angle where Larvitar's defense was weak.

"Larvitar, Dragon Dance, dodge!"

"Yoji!"

Larvitar cried out loudly, its body showing some rhythmic movement as it started running on its short legs with this rhythmic feeling.

Dragon Dance?

Dragalge, being a Dragon-type Pokémon, couldn't use it, but Larvitar, being Rock and Ground-type, could?

"Dragalge, Sludge Bomb!"

The whip-like Aqua Tail was narrowly avoided by Larvitar, but the Sludge Bomb that immediately followed from Dragalge's mouth wasn't so easy.

Deep purple sludge laden with poison shot from Dragalge's mouth like a cannonball, rapidly firing toward Larvitar.

"Larvitar!"

Larvitar crossed its arms over its chest, its body faintly showing a metallic luster as it directly faced the Sludge Wave from Dragalge.

Bang!!

The little one was knocked back several steps.

Hm?

Drasna squinted, noticing the metallic coloring that had appeared on Larvitar's body earlier.

Was that Iron Defense?

But Iron Defense was a move that increased physical defense, while Sludge Bomb was a special attack...

"Yoji!"

Larvitar, having finally steadied itself, quickly shook its somewhat numb hands. All the poisonous sludge sticking to them was shaken off, with no intention of seeping in.

Drasna's pupils contracted slightly, then she understood.

So it was using Iron Defense's Steel-type characteristics to prevent poisoning?

Moreover...

This Larvitar was really tough!

Setting aside the poison, even with 4x resistance, Larvitar taking a direct hit and only staggering?

If it were a Tyranitar, Drasna wouldn't be surprised.

Was this really just a Larvitar?

However...

"It's not that simple." Drasna became serious again.

And this time, it was Johan's turn to be surprised, because... poison still spread across Larvitar's body, not from the frontal Sludge Wave, but from the water currents Dragalge had left on the ground while moving!

The water was poisoned?

Poison spread up from its legs.

A Dragon-type Elite Four who was also so good with poison...

"Larvitar, Rock Slide!"

Relying on the speed boost from Dragon Dance, Larvitar steadied itself and immediately counterattacked.

Large rocks flew toward Dragalge's head.

"Dragalge, split it with Aqua Tail!"

Water currents swirled to create a barrier.

Bang!!

The rock shattered instantly, and Dragalge didn't take much damage. When it looked toward Larvitar again, it found the little one had already raised one foot high.

It fell.

Rumble rumble—

The entire ground shook violently, as if the earth was venting its fury. A crack rapidly split from beneath Larvitar's foot, reaching Dragalge in the blink of an eye.

This power...

Earthquake? Fissure?

No, it was Stomp!

Rock Slide had missed, so Stomp's power directly doubled!

And after doubling, Stomp's power was fifty percent greater than Earthquake!

"Dragalge, Waterfall—go up!"

Drasna reacted quickly. Dragalge immediately surged with water, ascending like climbing a waterfall, trying to avoid the impact of this Stomp.

However.

Water was surging upward, but water was also continuously flowing down into the ground cracks.

Boom!!

The Ground-type energy that erupted dealt considerable damage to Dragalge.

"Yoji!"

Seeing this, Larvitar excitedly clenched its fists, cheering for itself, but after the shout, its eyes squinted in pain.

Poisoned.

"Don't let your guard down—it's far from over."

Johan's voice echoed in Larvitar's mind.

After all, the little one was too far behind Drasna's Dragalge in level. Even with Ground-type's double effectiveness against Dragalge, it couldn't one-shot kill Dragalge.

Letting it out now was more for "leveling up."

Larvitar nodded heavily, enduring the gradually spreading pain from the poison in its body as it kept its eyes fixed on the dust raised by Stomp.

The next second, Johan's voice exploded in its ear.

"Protect!"

"Yoji!"

The current Larvitar was no longer the little one that had just been born not long ago. Its coordination and chemistry with Johan was very high. Just as the words rang out, it raised a green barrier.

Boom—

A terrifying water column erupted from the rising dust.

This was clearly the Water-type ultimate move, Hydro Pump!

Crack!

Under the rushing water's impact, Larvitar's Protect barrier shattered.

"Dragalge, Scald!"

Drasna waved her hand, no longer daring to underestimate Larvitar in the slightest.

After the dust settled, the somewhat exhausted Dragalge continued spitting water, but this time it was scalding hot water!

[Scald: Sprays the opponent with scalding hot water, with a chance to inflict burn status!]

Larvitar was a typical physical attacker. The poison status was manageable—it could barely endure it—but burn...

"Larvitar, Roar!"

"Yoji—!!"

Larvitar pointed at Dragalge and roared without mercy, releasing sound waves that seemed to form circles, lowering Dragalge's Special Attack.

At the same time.

A red beam shot out, hitting Larvitar before the hot water could reach it.

Pokémon switch!

Johan gripped the Poké Ball, looking at the heavily panting Dragalge, nodding slightly as he spoke to Larvitar inside the ball:

"You did very well."

To fight like this against an Elite Four's main Pokémon in pseudo-legendary cub form was already quite successful for Larvitar.

Moreover, Drasna wasn't just any Elite Four—she was the final Elite Four member of the Kalos region!

If they continued fighting, Larvitar might not necessarily be without fighting capability, but this was just casual sparring—there was no need to go that far.

Watching the recalled Larvitar, Drasna couldn't help frowning.

After brief hesitation, she chose not to switch.

Forcing Johan to switch Pokémon first gave her the advantage and initiative.

Johan put away the Poké Ball containing Larvitar and took out a second one.

"Go, Tinkaton!"

"Cha!"

In the red light, the hammer-wielding Tinkaton made a brilliant entrance, raising its hammer toward the opposing Dragalge.

Hey, hello there!

Steel and Fairy-type Tinkaton had an extreme type advantage over Dragalge.

But...

"Dragalge, Scald again!"

Splash splash—

Steaming hot water surged again.

"Cha!"

What goes around comes around!

Tinkaton spun its wrist, and the seemingly massive hammer was easily thrown out.

The scalding water met the metal hammer.

Bang!!

A gap was forcibly torn through the water stream, heading straight for Dragalge.

"Dodge!"

Dragalge almost instinctively moved aside. The terrifying hammer whooshed past its ear with a strong wind.

Seeing this, Dragalge secretly breathed a sigh of relief.

What a heavy hammer that could break through hot water with such impact—how much did it weigh, how much force was behind it?

However, before it could figure it out, Drasna's voice came again.

"Watch behind you! Dodge again!"

But this time, Dragalge obviously couldn't react in time.

Bang!!

The hammer that had clearly flown past it somehow came flying from behind again?

Tinkaton was standing in place without moving!

How was this done?

Drasna watched the hammer fly past Dragalge, then saw Tinkaton open its palm, and the hammer actually curved around behind Dragalge?

It curved!

How was this possible?

Drasna couldn't understand, and Dragalge was even more confused.

Using the hammer to execute Fake Out, putting it in a brief flinching state.

The outstretched Tinkaton also moved, striding forward as the hammer perfectly flew back into its hands!

Leaping high, falling heavily.

Ice Hammer!

Boom!!!

Ice crystals scattered instantly, the ground cracking in layers.

Dragalge was knocked out!

"Cha!"

Tinkaton raised its hammer with a triumphant expression like "a great victory with a great hammer."

At this moment, Johan, standing opposite Drasna and having witnessed the entire process, had a strange expression.

Good, good, good—

The hammer actually "came alive."

Meowth's hammer, right?

Xerneas's Fairy Aura infusion allowed Ninetales to somewhat learn Geomancy, while Tinkaton channeled that vast life energy into its hammer, and then...

The hammer became like this.

This was also Johan's first time seeing Tinkaton battle after it woke up, and his first time witnessing this.

Even though he'd already guessed this in his heart, he still felt it was somewhat strange.

Unexpected.

Not only unexpected for Drasna and Dragalge, but also for Johan.

"Cha~"

Tinkaton held the hammer handle with one hand and gently patted the hammerhead with the other.

Good hammer, obedient hammer~

Johan stared at the hammer for a while, carefully sensing with his aura until he confirmed the hammer made no "response," then he relaxed slightly.

Not alive.

But probably... Tinkaton had mastered some strange ability or technique.

Nothing else to say.

That move just now—the boomerang hammer—was quite cool.

However, after this, Drasna would definitely be on guard.

She'd wanted Dragalge to help expand her advantage, but instead got caught off guard. Not only did she fail to expand the advantage, but she fell into a disadvantage.

Steel + Fairy was hard to handle...

Drasna took a light breath, silently thinking and reviewing.

After brief consideration, she took out a Poké Ball and threw it again.

"Go, Noivern!"

A black and purple bat-like Pokémon appeared in the air above the field, flapping its wings. White fur around its neck swayed in the wind, and its huge ears were extremely eye-catching like two sound amplifiers.

"Noivern, Flying and Dragon-type Sound Wave Pokémon. It has a violent temperament and is hot-blooded, but also has a side that's friendly to humans. In darkness, it can even make Hydreigon fear it, Rotom!"

Johan was obviously familiar with Noivern, as Ash had one in the anime—very cool and liked to show off, but was unfortunately sent to Professor Oak after the Kalos journey ended, as usual.

"Another 'Lance's Delight Dragon'..." Johan murmured.

Flying and Dragon-type Noivern had no type advantage whatsoever against Tinkaton.

Of course, as a Flying-type Pokémon, when facing opponents that couldn't fly, its flexibility and mobility were inherently advantageous, especially since Noivern was incredibly fast.

Just...

"Cha!"

Seeing the Noivern that appeared in the air above the field, Tinkaton's eyes lit up as it turned to look at Johan, pointing at the sky.

A bird! Look, such a big bird!

"Gaah—!!"

This was heard by Noivern, which immediately roared angrily.

You're the bird! Your whole family are birds!

Hey, good hearing.

Tinkaton didn't mind, just lightly rubbing the hammer handle, eyes full of eagerness.

Bird or not, you don't get to decide—you'll have to ask my hammer!

The battle continued!

The sandstorm kept flying.

"Tinkaton, Rock Slide!" Johan immediately waved his hand.

Crack!!

The rocks that Larvitar had broken from the ground earlier saved Tinkaton considerable effort. It directly grabbed a large piece with one hand and threw it out, then gripped the hammer handle with both hands, drawing an arc.

Bang—

The rock shot out like a cannonball, heading straight for Noivern.

"Noivern, Boomburst!"

Drasna also knew the key to this battle—Noivern absolutely couldn't get close to the ground.

Buzz—

Noivern's two ears glowed white, then a terrifying sound wave burst forth. The surrounding air vibrated violently, as if everything in the sound wave's path would be crushed.

Crack crack crack—

The rock Tinkaton had thrown cracked and broke into small pieces under this powerful sound wave's impact, finally being shattered to powder.

The sound wave's power didn't diminish after destroying the rock, continuing to impact toward Tinkaton.

"Cha!"

Tinkaton immediately raised its hammer to protect itself.

However, sound waves were pervasive. Though the hammer blocked some of it, Tinkaton still endured the sound wave's impact, temporarily experiencing some ringing in its ears.

Must say...

Johan seemed to have discovered a bug in real Pokémon battles.

Moves like Noivern's Boomburst—after such a bombardment, Pokémon would likely fall into brief ear-ringing states, so... wouldn't trainers' commands be unheard?

"Gaah!!"

The flapping Noivern grinned.

Let's see you call it a bird or not—

Before it could finish being smug.

Whoosh—

Its ears suddenly picked up the sound of something cutting through air.

Hm?

The next moment.

Bang!!

A huge rock hit Noivern squarely on the head.

What was going on?

Hadn't the rock already been shattered?

Noivern was confused.

"Noivern, dodge quickly!"

Drasna's voice suddenly came.

Whoosh—

Another sound of cutting air.

This time, Noivern finally reacted, dodging to the side as a rock flew past where it had been.

Rock?

Fortunately, its peripheral vision finally noticed the situation below.

"Cha! Cha!"

Tinkaton looked excited, swinging its hammer with one hand while holding a rock with the other, throwing out another piece.

At Tinkaton's feet was a pile of rocks of various sizes, and it could grab another piece at any moment.

Wait!

When did you collect all these rocks?!

And your rock-throwing movements are way too skilled!

So skilled that Noivern's head started hurting.

Whoosh—whoosh—whoosh—

Noivern rapidly maneuvered in the air as rocks of various sizes were thrown up from below.

For a moment, the two sides seemed somewhat deadlocked.

Tinkaton was getting more and more excited, more and more happy.

Satisfying, so satisfying!

It had been so long since it had such a happy time hitting birds.

Whether it hit or not was another matter—the harder the target, the happier it got.

While Noivern was busy dodging in the air, it couldn't find a chance to counterattack—can you believe that?

Not just Noivern—even Drasna hadn't expected this battle to develop this way.

"Cha!!"

Tinkaton threw out another rock, glanced slightly after aiming, then quickly repeated its previous actions.

I can fail countless times, but as long as you get hit once and successfully trigger Rock Slide's additional effect, then hehe...

Johan faced Drasna's "shocked" gaze, covering his forehead slightly.

Cough...

This really wasn't trained—it was purely Tinkaton's instinct.

It was just that... their family's Tinkaton was a tiny bit better than other Tinkatons.

Actually, this was also related to Tinkaton receiving Xerneas's Fairy Aura baptism.

Though the hammer wasn't alive, Johan could feel that in Tinkaton's hands, the hammer seemed... lighter.

Previously, Tinkaton needed both hands gripping the handle to make rocks fly this fast, but now... one hand was enough.

One hand swinging the hammer, one hand throwing rocks—the attack speed naturally increased.

Nicknamed—Lance's Nemesis!

Even Ninetales might not match Tinkaton in purely countering "Flying-types."

This couldn't continue!

Drasna also understood the danger this posed to Noivern.

True, Noivern was fast and should be able to hold out for a while, but... constant defense and dodging would inevitably expose problems over time.

A long defense must fail!

Moreover.

Tinkaton and Johan wouldn't necessarily maintain this fighting style forever. Seeing it become an endurance battle between Noivern and Tinkaton.

They would definitely change tactics or rhythm at some point, and then... she and Noivern would be even more passive.

Rather than that, it was better to...

Drasna's eyes sharpened as she waved her hand vigorously. "Noivern, Boomburst!"

Feeling Drasna's momentum and awakening, Noivern found an angle to avoid a rock, then suddenly turned to release a terrifying sound wave impact.

It shattered another rock that was about to get close into powder, forcibly enduring a rock hitting its wing while struggling to maintain its form.

"Tsk." Johan and Tinkaton both clicked their tongues simultaneously.

Elite Four members were indeed Elite Four members.

The timing was perfectly calculated.

Tinkaton disappointedly put down an ice crystal it had secretly condensed. This was something it had gathered using Ice Hammer while throwing rocks, planning to catch Noivern off guard, but the opponent started counterattacking after taking a hit.

However.

Counterattacking was good!

Better than constantly circling in the sky.

"Roar—!!"

Noivern roared, flapping its wings while releasing terrifying sound waves and diving down toward Tinkaton from above.

Close combat time!

"Cha!"

Tinkaton gripped the hammer handle with both hands, the hammer glowing with faint pink light.

"Noivern!"

At this moment, Drasna shouted, intense red light bursting from her hands.

Hm?

Mega Evolution?

Noivern?

No, that's not right!

It was... a Z-Move!

After brief confusion, Johan suddenly realized that Drasna had chosen to use a Z-Move at this moment?

The timing was perfect—truly catching him off guard.

The power released by the Z-Crystal was channeled from Drasna to Noivern.

The Boomburst Noivern was releasing gradually faded, and an incredibly hot flame suddenly surged from its mouth!

Inferno Overdrive!

Damn!

It was even a Fire-type enhanced Z-Move?!

This round.

This round was truly getting shown up by Drasna.

Earlier, Johan and Tinkaton had caught her off guard, and now Drasna and Noivern were returning the favor.

A huge, blazing hot fireball flew toward Tinkaton.

The red fireball reflected even Tinkaton's hammer in fiery red, the scorching heat making Tinkaton's lips dry and mouth sticky.

"Protect!"

Johan's voice timely echoed in Tinkaton's mind.

As an aura user, the biggest advantage was that aura allowed him to observe the entire battlefield and give commands promptly.

As for Drasna not having aura while Johan did—was this cheating?

If I don't use my advantages, wouldn't all my preparation be wasted?

Buzz—

A green barrier appeared on the field for the second time.

Noticing the faint green glow beneath the blazing fireball, Drasna knew Tinkaton had reacted.

She secretly admired the quick reaction of Tinkaton and Johan.

Worthy of being called "Teacher Johan."

However, facing a Z-Move, even "Protect" couldn't completely block it!

Boom!!

The blazing fireball crashed down.

Crack—

A crisp sound came from within the flames as the Protect barrier shattered. The raging flames definitely dealt considerable damage to Tinkaton.

"Noivern, Gust!"

Seizing the gap when the Protect barrier broke, Drasna commanded again.

Fire borrowed wind's momentum.

Though Inferno Overdrive had been released, the flame's burning hadn't ended. With a helping Gust, let the flames become even more fierce!

Of course, controlling the wind's intensity was also necessary—if the wind was too strong, the fire would be extinguished.

Noivern flew beside the burning flames, flapping its wings to stir up wind.

Whoosh—

But just then.

A black shadow suddenly shot out from the flames!

Thud!!

It was the hammer!

It hit Noivern squarely on the head with a clear ringing sound. Noivern was hit dizzy, and the hammer bounced away, caught by Tinkaton as it charged out of the flames.

The next moment.

Tinkaton leaped up, taking advantage of Noivern's brief daze to ride on its back, grabbing one ear while gritting its teeth and raising the hammer.

Play Rough!

Bang—

A burst of cartoon-like smoke with peculiar patterns immediately rose.

"Still this energetic?" Drasna hadn't expected Tinkaton to break out of the flames so quickly.

A few seconds later.

"Cha!!"

Noivern crashed to the ground, its face bruised and battered. Tinkaton rode on its back, one hand grabbing an ear while the other held the hammer against its mouth.

Submit or not!

Noivern's heart was bitter.

Big sister, you've practically shoved the hammer into my mouth—how do you expect me to talk?

Do I still want my teeth?

Obviously.

Though Inferno Overdrive had been Protected against, the damage it dealt to Tinkaton was still significant, though not fatal.

Moreover.

Johan also noticed that some of the burn marks on Tinkaton's body were slowly healing.

The vast life energy from Xerneas actually gave Tinkaton an effect similar to carrying "Leftovers"?

Drasna breathed out a long sigh, taking out a Poké Ball to recall Noivern, who was being ridden by Tinkaton.

Both sides specialized in catching each other off guard, but she still fell behind.

In pure command and reaction, there were some gaps.

The stronger one became, the more one could feel the benefits brought by powers like aura and psychic abilities.

Specialized in information advantages.

With Noivern recalled, Tinkaton hurriedly examined its hammer, seeing no signs of melting, and patted its chest with relief.

Good, good...

"Well done, Tinkaton." Johan praised.

"Cha?"

Tinkaton turned its head with an extremely loud voice, putting its hand by its ear and leaning in to listen.

What did you say? Can't hear you, speak louder, didn't you eat?

Johan: "..."

He lightly adjusted his glasses, somewhat exasperated.

Must say.

It was good he knew aura—otherwise, if it were someone else with a Pokémon, if the Pokémon didn't have certain autonomous abilities, it would be hard to say.

Sound wave attacks really had something.

Seeing Tinkaton's cute appearance, the originally stern-faced Drasna couldn't help but "pfft" laugh out loud.

"Teacher Johan, your Pokémon are all more adorable than the last."

"Ha, haha..." Johan laughed dryly.

If you knew how much trouble this bunch could cause normally, you wouldn't so easily use the word "adorable" to describe them.

# 644: Order God? No! Top-Level Investigator! (Two-in-One Chapter)

Noivern hadn't lost its fighting ability, but honestly... it was pretty much done for.

For Drasna, through these two battles, she had felt the intensity of battling against Johan.

It wasn't that Johan's Pokémon were overwhelmingly stronger than hers, but rather she felt the gap between trainers.

Let's not even talk about Tinkaton—its type advantage over Noivern was something that Noivern's flying ability offset to some degree. While Tinkaton was indeed stronger in raw power than Noivern, if you really had to say it was strong enough to completely dominate, that wasn't quite the case.

But the way the battle played out did have some dominating characteristics.

Even when Drasna used a Z-Move to make a desperate play, it was still neutralized by Johan's commands and Tinkaton's own "unique qualities."

As for Larvitar, that was even more obvious.

Larvitar was definitely not as strong as Dragalge in terms of pure power, yet it managed to fight Dragalge almost to a standstill through Johan's commands, tactics, and Larvitar's own inherent "special qualities."

Pokémon battles were based on two components.

One part was naturally the Pokémon's own raw strength, which was an important factor in determining how a Pokémon battle would unfold—in other words, this determined the lower limit.

The second part was the trainer's commanding ability. The more capable the trainer, the more they could demonstrate the importance of the trainer's role.

Based on tactics, on-the-spot adaptability, one's own emotions, the bond with Pokémon, and so on, these determined the upper limit of battles.

Being able to turn around Pokémon battles where one's Pokémon were weaker than the opponent's through tactics and adaptability—this was the important role of trainers.

In the previous two battles, Drasna clearly felt that as a trainer, she was inferior to Johan.

"What a rather discouraging result," Drasna shook her head.

However, the battle had to continue. Giving up halfway wasn't something a strong-willed Elite Four member would do.

So, Drasna threw out her final Poké Ball, summoning her ace Pokémon.

"I'm counting on you, Altaria!"

A Pokémon with wings like fluffy cotton or clouds appeared—it was the beloved Altaria!

"As expected."

Seeing Drasna's final Pokémon, Johan clicked his tongue and muttered to himself.

Unlike Drasna experiencing the role and gap between trainers, Johan's main purpose in agreeing to this battle was to better understand changes in his Pokémon.

Specifically, to understand the condition and situation of Tinkaton and Ninetales after receiving Xerneas's Fairy Aura baptism.

So.

Having seen Tinkaton, Johan was also quite looking forward to the changes in Ninetales.

"Come back, Tinkaton."

"Cha?!"

Tinkaton placed its hand beside its ear and tilted its head, straining to hear what Johan was saying.

What are you saying?!

It shouted extra loud.

Johan: "..."

He really felt like he should ask Drasna for some medical fees after this battle.

In the end, Johan still took out a Poké Ball and recalled Tinkaton.

In its place was...

"Oowoo~~"

The graceful and agile Ninetales stepped onto the messy battlefield with elegant steps.

Altaria was a beloved Pokémon for its beautiful appearance, but if we're really comparing, our Ninetales was not only not inferior, but actually superior.

"Phew—"

Seeing Tinkaton leave, Drasna breathed a slight sigh of relief.

When Noivern was flying in the sky, it was in quite a situation. She still clearly remembered it, and she was really a bit afraid that Altaria would face the same predicament.

To be honest.

Even facing a Fairy-type and Ice-type combination that absolutely countered Dragon-type and Flying-type Pokémon, Drasna felt a bit reluctant to fight Johan's Tinkaton.

It was too frustrating.

Moreover.

Altaria facing Ninetales wasn't completely at a type disadvantage.

She closed her eyes and gently covered the ceremonial ornament on her chest with her hand, specifically the gem in the center.

Buzz—

That gem immediately burst with brilliant rainbow light, overflowing from between her fingers.

"Altaria!"

Drasna opened her eyes again.

"Mega Evolution!"

"Chirp—"

Altaria spread its cloud-like wings, and the Mega Stone on its body resonated strongly with Drasna's Key Stone, instantly being enveloped in evolutionary light.

"Here comes the 'Dragon Traitor'..." Johan looked up at the Mega Evolving Altaria in mid-air and muttered.

As everyone knew, Altaria was a Dragon and Flying-type Humming Pokémon, but after Mega Evolution, its Flying-type would be replaced by Fairy-type.

That is to say, Mega Altaria would be a Dragon and Fairy-type Pokémon.

The nickname "Dragon Traitor" came from this.

"Chirp—!!"

A clear, ethereal cry echoed through the sky. The Mega Evolution light faded, the symbol of Mega Evolution flashed and disappeared, and what appeared before Johan and Ninetales was Mega Altaria!

With Mega Altaria's appearance, it could finally be said to be a match for Ninetales in a beauty contest.

More fluffy and dense white feathers made it look like an elf among the clouds, both agile and beautiful.

Speaking of which.

Actually, the Dragon-type Pokémon of the Kalos region... really had quite a few that weren't afraid of Fairy-types.

For example, the Mega Altaria before them, and the Dragalge from earlier.

Perhaps it was because they lived in a region with many Fairy-types that they "evolved" such abilities.

Of course, even if it was Mega Altaria, facing Fairy-type attacks, it would still take double damage—it just had more ways to deal with them than being completely helpless.

"Oowoo~"

Ninetales stood below, looking up at Mega Altaria in the sky, its azure eyes twinkling with light.

Snowflakes began falling from the sky, and soon turned into a raging blizzard.

Compared to Tinkaton, which could only throw rocks at flying Mega Altaria, Ninetales had much more flexible and free methods when facing the aerial Mega Altaria.

Drasna frowned slightly.

Snow weather.

Although snow weather didn't cause damage like Sandstorm, the extreme cold and temperature would still make Dragon-type Pokémon's bodies cool down, making them less agile.

So, she had to act quickly and decisively!

"Altaria, Dragon Dance!" Drasna waved her hand decisively, officially opening the curtain on this battle.

"Chirp!!"

A long cry echoed through the sky, and Dragon-type energy surged around Altaria as its momentum rapidly climbed.

Boosting Speed and Attack, accelerating the speed to determine victory.

While Mega Altaria was performing Dragon Dance, Ninetales, standing on the ground with all four paws, also began using a move.

"Geomancy!" Johan adjusted his glasses, looking forward with considerable anticipation.

Geomancy?

Drasna was stunned.

What move was that?

She saw.

Ninetales' snow-white body suddenly burst with brilliant rainbow light, and its paws touching the ground seemed to sense the pulse from the earth itself. That vibrant life force caused a circle of pink mist to emanate from its body.

Misty Terrain?

But why did it look different from the Misty Terrain she had seen before?

Ninetales' aura had an obvious boosting trend.

A stat-boosting move?

Drasna was somewhat confused, while Johan appeared quite excited.

"It really learned it."

Although the way it was performed looked quite different from Xerneas, and unlike Xerneas, who as the Life God would be accompanied by rich life energy, Ninetales didn't have those things.

But purely in terms of power boost, Ninetales got it!

This was enough!

Geomancy—through a period of power accumulation, it greatly boosted the user's Special Attack, Special Defense, and Speed!

This was a very impressive boost.

You have to know, the signature move of Dragon-type Pokémon, Dragon Dance, only brought one level boost each to Speed and Attack, but Geomancy brought six levels of boost in total!

Of course.

Dragon Dance was faster to execute and allowed movement, and many people's tactics even used Dragon Dance as a way to dodge opponent's move attacks.

While Geomancy required a longer accumulation time and couldn't move after execution, or the move would be interrupted.

But it was extremely compatible with Ninetales.

Because Ninetales... had excellent defensive capabilities while stationary!

Having already sensed a great threat from Ninetales, Drasna immediately launched a fierce attack the moment Mega Altaria's Dragon Dance ended.

"Altaria, Hyper Beam!"

"Chirp!!"

Mega Altaria let out a long cry, pink Fairy-type energy surged, and it immediately shot down toward Ninetales like a meteor.

Because after Mega Evolution, Altaria's ability would uniformly become "Pixilate," so the Hyper Beam it used, although originally a Normal-type move, became Fairy-type when executed, and its power was boosted to some degree.

However.

Bang—

Before Mega Altaria could impact Ninetales, it immediately hit a transparent barrier.

Aurora Veil!

"When did it use Aurora Veil?" Drasna was puzzled.

But fortunately, it only slightly hindered Mega Altaria's momentum.

Crack—

The Aurora Veil shattered.

Ninetales, standing on the ground, was completely exposed to Mega Altaria's attack.

"Tsk, not proficient enough," Johan couldn't help clicking his tongue.

Geomancy was powerful, but Ninetales had only learned it and never used it before, so the time it took was much longer than expected.

However, he believed that through frequent practice in the future, it should become more proficient, and the execution time would be faster.

By then, Ninetales could use stacked Aurora Veils to safely complete Geomancy—this was one of the reasons Johan said it was very compatible with this move.

Boom!!

The terrifying impact crashed down heavily, snow on the ground suddenly exploded, and Ninetales was sent flying, sliding on the ground for some distance before barely controlling its form.

"Ice walls?"

Drasna squinted, noticing that just as Mega Altaria was about to impact Ninetales, ice walls that suddenly rose had hindered it again.

So... although Ninetales had taken Hyper Beam's attack, Geomancy had also successfully accumulated!

"Oowoo—!!"

It half-raised its head, azure light seeming to dye Ninetales' snow-white fur into blue-white colors, and its aura reached its peak at this moment!

The next second.

Buzz buzz buzz—

Aurora Veils fell one after another, so fast that both Drasna and Mega Altaria were speechless.

No wait.

Johan lightly pressed his hat brim.

Cough.

Our Ninetales was still as cautious as ever, still the same battle style, even though it had already gained considerable power.

"Altaria, Defog!"

Whoosh—

Mega Altaria flapped its wings vigorously, stirring up winds mixed with ice and snow, making the Aurora Veils in the field immediately unstable.

Defog could clear away foggy weather and moves like Light Screen, Reflect, and Aurora Veil, and even clear terrain—it was a very overpowered move.

Drasna obviously had plenty of experience dealing with Ice-type blizzard Aurora Veil and Fairy-type Misty Terrain combinations.

"Oowoo!"

Ninetales puffed out its cheeks, its azure eyes showing a serious expression.

The Aurora Veils were cleared—this made things... unstable.

"Ninetales, Moonblast!"

Johan didn't immediately have Ninetales use its already powerful Ice-type moves, but wanted to first see how its Fairy-type moves had changed.

"Oowoo~~~"

A beam of moonlight descended vertically, and the gathered moonlight became Ninetales' power.

"Altaria, we'll use Moonblast too!" Drasna didn't choose to retreat, still carrying out the strategy she had set from the beginning—quick battle, quick decision!

Both sides' moon powers formed light orbs in front of their respective Pokémon, then flew toward each other.

But once the moves were executed, Drasna immediately felt the gap between Mega Altaria and Ninetales in the same move—quite significant.

This kind of head-to-head confrontation would definitely result in Mega Altaria's defeat, so...

Drasna gritted her teeth and said coldly:

"Altaria, Hyper Beam!"

Rather than sitting and waiting for Ninetales' Moonblast to break through Mega Altaria's Moonblast and then hit it, it was better to take the initiative.

"Chirp!!!"

Mega Altaria understood the previous disadvantage in the clash and the gap between itself and the opponent, so... it could only get close for melee combat, perhaps bringing some trouble to this ranged-focused Ninetales.

So it once again transformed into a pink giant bird, charging toward Moonblast.

"The Fairy-type moves and power have both improved considerably, and this is still without fully digesting it..." Johan, also watching the battle situation, had already seen results that satisfied him.

Previously, Ninetales was strong, but its Ice-type focus was much greater than its Fairy-type focus, making the two types unbalanced.

But now, it was about right.

Although the Fairy-type was still a bit behind, as long as Ninetales was given a bit more time to digest, it should be able to catch up.

"About right..." Johan was quite pleased.

And quite grateful.

Grateful that Elite Four Drasna had given such an excellent testing opportunity.

Since that was the case...

Johan took a deep breath, his expression suddenly became stern, and he said in a low voice: "Ninetales, Absolute Zero!"

Crack crack crack—

A breath of cold air gently exhaled from Ninetales' mouth, and out of nowhere came the sound of ice forming.

Then, frost seemed to spread through the air, rapidly sweeping toward the charging Mega Altaria.

Just look.

Frost formed on Mega Altaria's cloud-like wings, and it rapidly increased.

"This Ice-type power?" Drasna was somewhat shocked.

The moves that Teacher Johan's Ninetales used were all ones she had never heard of, but the power of these moves was truly a bit too impressive!

Mega Altaria's speed dropped sharply, its impact force becoming obviously insufficient.

The key was.

The closer it got to Ninetales, the more it could feel the cold, that bone-chilling cold from outside to inside.

Mega Altaria was ultimately a Dragon-type Pokémon, and cold had too strong a restraining effect on it.

Moreover, it was Ninetales with a two-level Special Attack boost.

So when it braved the cold and charged to Ninetales' front... it had already become a living ice sculpture!

"Oowoo~"

Ninetales gently exhaled a breath of air—Absolute Zero took quite a bit of energy to execute.

However, for safety's sake, it still couldn't help but give Mega Altaria two more Freeze-Dry attacks.

At this point.

The battle was completely over!

To be honest.

Although Drasna had anticipated that she might lose, she really hadn't expected... to lose in such a manner.

Altaria directly frozen into an ice sculpture.

"Such powerful Ice-type moves." Drasna took out a Poké Ball and shot a red beam to recall Altaria.

Her serious and earnest demeanor also returned to her previous gentle, smiling appearance.

"Oowoo~~"

Ninetales trotted back to Johan's side.

Johan couldn't help but tighten his clothes.

His "cold resistance attribute" was higher than his "poison and paralysis resistance attributes" and was still at the edge, but he still felt cold.

When would this "deep blue point allocation" end...

Johan sighed and crouched down to gently stroke Ninetales' soft, smooth fur, taking out two energy cubes to restore stamina and putting them in the little one's mouth.

Don't look at how easily it won—the stamina consumption for Ninetales was actually quite significant.

"Oowoo~~"

Ninetales affectionately licked Johan's cheek.

"You and your Pokémon really have a very good relationship." Drasna walked up to see this scene and said.

"Perhaps this is the reason you and your Pokémon can display such strength."

Johan gently stroked Ninetales and smiled: "It's all the little ones working hard."

Drasna shook her head.

The Pokémon's hard work was certainly important, but the trainer's cultivation and commands were equally crucial—Johan was being modest.

However, she didn't continue to delve deeper into this topic, but said: "With your strength, you should be able to try challenging the Champion."

Champion?

Johan laughed dryly.

"Still far from it."

Setting aside other things, just talking about battling Alder, without unconventional powers, Johan felt he couldn't win.

Actually, Gengar and Ninetales could be said to have the strength to face Champions head-on, and Dragonite, if it went into Outrage, could also fight, but his other Pokémon were still a bit lacking.

After Tinkaton completely digested Xerneas's "gift," it should be able to touch the Champion threshold. Urshifu and Ceruledge... would depend on going all out.

These were two who temporarily needed to go all out to infinitely raise their upper limits.

It seemed like...

He needed to find opportunities to strengthen Urshifu and Ceruledge again.

As for Larvitar...

Continue eating heartily for a while longer.

Of course, his words in Drasna's ears just sounded like modesty.

In Drasna's view, the Ninetales that had just erupted with power should not be inferior to ordinary Champions' ace Pokémon, and she also knew that Johan's ace was Gengar.

It was just that she didn't know that what she saw was Ninetales after using Geomancy—which was enhanced.

But honestly, the role Ninetales could play in "specific" battles could indeed be stronger than Gengar.

"I feel like Drake from your Hoenn region might not be able to beat you either." Drasna seemed quite familiar with Drake.

Perhaps because they were both Dragon-type Elite Four?

But Drake was much older than Drasna, and Drake's strength should be at the Champion threshold in Johan's opinion, possibly just slightly weaker than Alder. He was one of Hoenn's current "faces."

Drake didn't want to be Champion, otherwise the current Hoenn League Champion would probably be him.

"Drake is my superior." Johan smiled.

"What's wrong with superiors? They can still be battled." Drasna said teasingly.

"Uh..."

Johan's expression was awkward.

Seeing his embarrassed look, Drasna couldn't help but laugh out loud.

After laughing, she suddenly showed a serious expression and asked: "How about it, are you interested in coming to work in our Kalos? I could... make you Champion?"

Johan: "..."

No way.

Big sister, you're just an Elite Four, you can appoint Champions?

Moreover...

Johan increasingly felt like he was becoming a hot commodity, with people inviting him wherever he went. Although he wouldn't agree, it was quite satisfying.

"Cough, I'm a Hoenn person."

"What's wrong with being from Hoenn? My hometown is still Celestic Town in Sinnoh."

Johan: "..."

This way, we can't have a conversation.

"Alright then."

Drasna actually was just trying, and really making Johan stay in Kalos to be Champion... she really didn't have that authority.

Moreover, Kalos was different from Unova—Unova was somewhat in a green-and-yellow transition period, while their Kalos still had Diantha.

It was just that Diantha... was busy filming movies all the time.

But that was normal too—their Kalos region trainers all had side businesses, which had almost become a "Kalos tradition."

"Then..."

Drasna stood on tiptoe and like an elder, gently patted Johan's head, tilting her head with curved eyes and smiling cheerfully:

"Work hard, and try to marry our little Cynthia to Hoenn someday."

Johan: "..."

Drasna waved at Johan and left with satisfaction.

You could see that although she lost the battle, she was quite satisfied with the fight.

The Pokémon world was like this.

If you liked each other, you'd battle. If you didn't like each other, you'd also battle. Winning was naturally happy, and losing wasn't a big deal either—as long as you enjoyed the process and had fun.

It was a bit like card players playing cards.

Winning or losing didn't matter—the key was that you had to give me a chance to draw cards!

"That's not right."

Looking at Drasna disappearing from view, Johan suddenly reacted.

Wait, you haven't paid the medical fees yet!

And after finishing a battle, shouldn't you drop some coins or something?

But seeing that Drasna had already "run away," Johan didn't chase after her.

Fortunately, today he had already gotten a Dragonium Z and a complete set of various Poké Balls—the harvest was quite abundant.

More importantly, he had tested Tinkaton and Ninetales' abilities and their changes after receiving Xerneas's Fairy Aura baptism. Overall, he was very satisfied.

[That was quite an interesting human...] The Zygarde core suddenly sighed.

Hm?

Johan looked toward his shoulder.

"You haven't left yet?"

The Zygarde core: "???"

"Cough, I thought that after Xerneas fell asleep and Yveltal left, you had already left too."

So you've been invisible—no weight at all, and I can't sense it with aura either.

But Johan was actually quite envious of Zygarde.

Not that he coveted its strength—this kind of first-class legendary Pokémon, unless it was willing or didn't have so-called "divine duties," there was absolutely no possibility of capture, only making friends.

What he envied was Zygarde's ability to live perfectly without needing to eat, just needing care.

If he had a Pokémon like this... Johan felt he could wake up laughing from dreams.

[I just felt that through you, I could get a good channel for observing humans.]

The Zygarde core snorted coldly.

Johan shrugged.

If the Zygarde core didn't want to leave on its own, he wouldn't drive it away—it was a legendary Pokémon after all.

"Speaking of which..." Johan's mind suddenly stirred, thinking of something. "Do you know if there are any shiny, or rather, differently colored Zygarde?"

White Gundam felt cooler than the original black-green Gundam...

[Differently colored Zygarde?]

But hearing Johan's question, the Zygarde core was stunned.

[What do you mean? Have you seen one?]

"You haven't seen one?"

One person and one core stared at each other for a while, and Johan was the first to give up.

"Alright, I probably saw it in a dream."

The Zygarde core: "..."

Zygarde's reaction made him somewhat puzzled.

He clearly remembered there was a white Zygarde in "Horizons," along with a black Rayquaza...

Could it be that this wasn't the same Pokémon world?

He started walking toward Laverre City, preparing to go to the Pokémon Center to help the little ones recover.

On the way.

"Speaking of which, Zygarde, with your abilities, you should be able to observe some Pokémon hunters, right?" Johan asked while walking.

[Naturally.]

"You don't interfere?"

[That's not my responsibility—it's my partner's job.]

So... this was one of the reasons the other Zygarde core was so unfriendly to humans?

Witnessing too many behaviors that destroyed the environment and balance.

"Then you can sense them, right?"

[Some of them.]

"Great, you're an excellent Zygarde."

The Zygarde core: "..."

This feeling of coaxing a child was what?

But honestly...

[Of course!]

The Zygarde core slightly raised its head.

Laverre City Pokémon Center.

"Cha?"

Tinkaton's loud voice, even with the good soundproofing in each room of the Pokémon Center, was still a bit hard to contain.

"Ka-kaah."

Gengar covered its ears with its hands and bared its teeth at Tinkaton.

Good grief, so you want to compete with me for the high notes?

The other little ones in the room also covered their ears at the same time.

Tinkaton scratched its head, realizing it seemed to have lost control again.

But fortunately, everyone didn't seem to blame it. Ninetales even gently touched Tinkaton's head with its tail, signaling that it was okay.

Of course, ignoring the two tails that had blocked ears, the effect would be even better.

"Gengar, calm down. If it really doesn't work, just pierce your eardrums and you'll be fine."

Sitting at the desk, Johan said calmly, as if joking.

He thought of an anime he had seen before—forgot which one—but when facing enemy sound attacks, they directly pierced their own eardrums to block it, which was somewhat... outrageous.

"Ka-kaah?"

Gengar believed it was true and just wanted to confirm one thing.

Could it heal after piercing?

However, Johan didn't give any response.

Gengar immediately moved forward, removed the earplugs from Johan's ears, and then... put them in its own ears.

"Ka-kaah kaah kaah kaah~~"

The little fat one laughed with hands on hips and head thrown back.

I'm much smarter than you, hehe~

"I should have asked Drasna for some medical fees..." Johan rubbed his temples.

Fortunately, Tinkaton had consumed some stamina from the daytime battle and was somewhat tired. Under Ninetales' comfort, the two little ones soon fell asleep hugging each other.

"That should be about it, right?" Johan looked toward the Zygarde core on the desk with its head held high.

[Mm.]

The Zygarde core nodded slightly.

In front of Johan on the paper were recorded Pokémon hunter group information and bases that could be collected through the Zygarde core and its "cells" spread throughout the Kalos region.

Johan was very satisfied with this.

[You're not planning to go beat them up one by one, are you?]

The Zygarde core couldn't help asking.

Johan put down his pen, took a sip of coffee, and smiled:

"Who said I was going to beat them up one by one myself?"

[Hm?]

"Humans can actually be quite united sometimes." Johan took out his phone and flipped to the "Kalos Region International Police Task Force," which contained the mid-to-high-level International Police responsible for the Kalos region.

Click—

He took a photo of the paper and uploaded it to the group.

Then, with a serious expression, he pressed the voice input button: "These locations have an 80-90% probability of having Pokémon hunter group bases."

Very quickly.

The group flashed with a series of "Received" messages.

And with his single sentence, International Police throughout the Kalos region, League Police, and even Gym Leaders all sprang into action.

When encountering tough nuts to crack, even Elite Four might be deployed.

According to the system established by the League Alliance, Johan, as one of the few "Police Superintendents," had the authority to mobilize Elite Four-level "nuclear weapons" in special moments or wartime.

This was the benefit of "being an official."

With one command, subordinates would handle most matters.

And he could enjoy the credit.

This "social atmosphere" had finally reached Johan.

This day.

Was the beginning of a nightmare for Pokémon hunter groups in the Kalos region.

Zygarde, Order God?

No—top-level investigator!

----------

Powerstones?

# 645: "Gone Completely Wild" (Two-in-One Chapter)

Distortion World.

On a relatively large inverted island.

Crash—

Diamonds of various sizes scattered like a waterfall, clattering as they fell all over the ground.

"Roar!!!"

Giratina's impotent rage echoed freely throughout the Distortion World, stirring up waves of invisible ripples.

Damn it!

Giratina looked up to the sky.

Was it easy for it?

It had spent so much time and energy to finally piece together this "diamond screen," and it... collapsed!

Damn it, these diamonds of all sizes were almost all different, and to piece together this complete "diamond screen" without gaps had been so difficult for it.

The result.

Just when it was about to be completed, the thing actually collapsed!

After its impotent rage, Giratina rubbed its chin.

Saliva really didn't work.

Couldn't stick it together.

As the possessor of "antimatter energy," destroying things was a matter of minutes for it—antimatter could rush through and not even leave residue behind.

But making it stick things together... that was really making things difficult for a Pokémon.

It needed to find something with strong adhesive properties that wouldn't affect the diamond's essence, otherwise when Johan came asking for diamonds later, having them covered in glue wouldn't work.

Giratina looked around.

Well, it had to admit that in the Distortion World, there definitely wasn't such a thing.

After brief consideration.

Giratina tore open the space in front of it, the opening revealing a corner of the Pokémon world.

Then it would go to the Pokémon world to look.

Giratina flicked its tail.

It disappeared from the Distortion World.

Pokémon World, Kalos region, Laverre City.

"Fashion Design Contest?"

Johan, who was preparing to bid farewell to Valerie, saw her packing in her clothing store.

Speaking of which.

Valerie, as a Gym Leader, spent more time in the clothing store than in the gym.

Oh, this was Kalos, so never mind then.

"That's right." Valerie neatly packed away her carefully designed clothing, then covered it with professional bags.

"It just happens to coincide with a special festival, and I heard there will be fireworks tonight too." Valerie said.

Festival?

Fireworks show?

Johan's eyes lit up slightly.

Summer Fireworks Festival!

"Are you interested too, Teacher Johan? There should be some other competition too, oh right, the Pokémon Catch Race!"

As someone in the fashion design industry, Valerie was most concerned with fashion design competitions, and wasn't very interested in Pokémon catching competitions, since she was quite picky about catching Pokémon anyway.

"Ka-kaah?!"

Gengar grabbed Johan's shoulder with one hand, poking its head out from behind him.

Competition?

Pokémon Catch Race!

When they first came to the Kalos region, they had originally wanted to participate in the "Pokémon Triathlon" competition, but because it conflicted with Diancie's matter, they didn't get to compete.

Hearing about another competition, Gengar immediately became excited.

Since it was a competition... there would definitely be nice prizes, right?

Johan was more interested in what Valerie called the "fireworks festival."

Summer fireworks festival, clear night sky dotted with stars, warm evening, refreshing ice cream, lively atmosphere, and blooming fireworks...

Mew would definitely love it, right?

He had originally promised to take Mew to participate in Kanaz Pokémon Academy's Spring Festival, but missed it because of the "World Coronation Series," so this summer fireworks evening could give it some compensation.

"If you're interested, Teacher Johan, we could go together~" Valerie smiled.

"Ka-kaah! Ka-kaah!"

Before Johan could answer, Gengar nodded repeatedly, acting like it had agreed for him.

"Let me make a phone call." Johan said to Valerie.

"Of course."

Walking to the store entrance, Johan took out his phone and dialed a number.

"What's wrong?" From the phone came a voice with some laziness and magnetic warmth.

"You're not still in bed, are you?" Hearing that voice, Johan couldn't help but laugh, asking teasingly.

"Mm—"

Then he heard rustling sounds and stretching movements.

"Training felt good last night, so I trained a bit late." Cynthia curled up in her blanket.

After laughing for a while, Johan asked: "Fireworks festival, interested?"

"Fireworks festival?"

Cynthia immediately sat up from bed, her Jigglypuff pajamas bouncing out.

"Garrr?"

"Lucaa?"

In the room.

Garchomp, who had also trained late last night and was still resting, raised its head, half-squinting with some unfriendly intent in its eyes—it heard a familiar voice.

Meanwhile, Lucario, who was organizing the books scattered around the room, also looked over.

Fireworks festival?

They really hadn't participated in one this year.

Today had been a bit too busy.

Since the "World Coronation Series" ended, Cynthia and they had spent most of their time training, only leaving Celestic Town and Mt. Coronet during the Arceus incident.

Normally, aside from beating up Flint, they really didn't have much entertainment.

"Where?" Cynthia couldn't help asking.

You could tell she was quite interested in the fireworks festival too.

Johan lightly patted his forehead, covered the phone receiver and turned to look at Valerie in the store: "Miss Valerie, where did you say the place was?"

"Oh, Fula City." Valerie, who was almost done packing her clothes, said.

Johan nodded and said to Cynthia on the phone: "Fula City."

Hm?

Fula City?!

"Mm..."

Cynthia held the phone between her shoulder and ear, taking the laptop Lucario handed her, and after a quick search said:

"It really is, the Wind Festival in Fula City is coming up soon, not only fireworks festival, fashion design contest, Pokémon Catch Race..."

Fula City...

Johan didn't know that Fula City from the movie "The Power of Us" would be in the Kalos region.

After all, the "protagonist" Zeraora was a seventh-generation Pokémon, while Fula City's origin came from the second-generation legendary Lugia.

But...

It didn't matter anyway.

Johan didn't have much "resistance" to Fula City, since there weren't any legendary "disasters."

At most it would just be Lugia and Zeraora.

Lugia... Johan's relationship with it was quite "solid"—during the Arceus incident, Lugia had been called by him to "help out."

As for Zeraora...

It should be one of Johan's favorite Electric-type Pokémon.

In terms of strength, it shouldn't be unmanageable either.

"Do you have time? We could go to Fula City together to relax." Johan invited.

He knew Cynthia had been busy training recently, improving her strength.

He didn't know what level Cynthia had reached now.

"I've been quite busy recently, lots of things..." Cynthia stretched, her words carrying some deeper meaning.

And Johan obviously understood, saying: "This humble one sincerely invites Her Majesty the Queen to grace us with her presence."

"Since you're inviting me so sincerely, then I'll 'reluctantly' make a trip." Cynthia laughed.

"I'll help you look for flight tickets."

"No need, I'll ride Garchomp over, should arrive before dinner."

Garchomp on the side: "?"

What happened to being reserved?

"Alright, be safe on the road."

Although with Cynthia's strength, if they encountered trouble, the other party should be the one to worry, Johan still reminded her.

"Mm."

Fula City.

A coastal city isolated by vast mountain forests.

Of course, that isolation was in the past—with the current level of technological development in the Pokémon world, there were plenty of ways to establish contact with Fula City.

For example, train tracks through the mountain forests, planes in the sky, and ships on the sea.

Although Laverre City wasn't exactly a coastal city, there were ports nearby, so Johan, Valerie, and Valerie's geishas chose to take a ship to Fula City.

Warm sunshine, rolling clouds, gentle sea breeze—Johan had taken off Valerie's custom outfit and changed into an Alolan floral shirt, sitting on the cruise ship's deck fishing.

"Gengar, Ceruledge, set up the barbecue grill, we'll have grilled fish later."

Johan, sitting under a parasol, said without turning his head.

"Ka-kaah!"

Gengar nodded and responded, then continued sitting in place, holding Pokémon playing cards, not moving.

Ceruledge did the same, responding but not moving.

Grilled fish?

They probably wouldn't be able to catch edible fish by the time the ship docked at Fula City port.

So this barbecue grill... might as well not set up.

"Ka-kaah~"

Gengar wrapped itself in its Spell Tag, gently patting Regieleki's shoulder.

Hey, what are you daydreaming about, it's your turn to play.

"Regi..."

Was Regieleki daydreaming?

It just didn't know what card to play.

Scratching its head, looking at the pair of "Tyranitar" in front of it, then glancing at its hand.

A pair of "Caterpie," one "Pidgeotto," two "Flareon," one "Eevee," one "Zubat," one...

"Cha~"

Tinkaton, sitting on its hammer, couldn't help reminding.

You can pass if you can't beat it.

"Eleki..."

Regieleki breathed a sigh of relief and nodded.

Pass!

"Ka-kaah~" Gengar grinned wickedly, about to continue playing.

"Vii!"

Victini suddenly interrupted it, signaling Gengar to wait.

"Ka-kaah~"

Gengar, holding only two cards left, looked at Victini's seventeen cards and didn't mind at all, gesturing.

Go ahead, I don't believe you can beat me in one turn with seventeen cards!

Then Victini's performance began.

Two "Rayquaza," one green one black, played!

A straight, "Nidoqueen," "Nidoking," "Nidorino"... six cards total.

Another straight, "Eevee," "Vaporeon," "Flareon"... eight cards total!

Holding the last "Caterpie," Victini looked around at Gengar, Tinkaton, and Regieleki, asking with a smile:

"Vii?"

Anyone want it?

"Ka-kaah?"

Gengar rubbed its eyes, using both hands to squeeze and stretch its head, as if it couldn't believe what it was seeing.

No way.

Seventeen cards, and you really can beat me in one turn?

"Vii!"

Seeing no reaction from the three little ones, Victini decisively threw out the last "Caterpie."

Victory!

It showed its fangs and made a "yeah" gesture.

Then it took energy cubes from the piles in front of Gengar, Tinkaton, and Regieleki, corresponding to their remaining card counts.

Victory Pokémon Victini had "completely dominated" at this moment!

Gengar was actually fine—it only had two cards left, so only lost two cubes. Tinkaton was okay too with seven cards, but Regieleki...

"Regi..."

Looking at its energy cube pile that had shrunk by more than ten again, Regieleki scratched its head.

No good, so itchy, felt like it was going to grow a brain.

Meanwhile.

"Got one! Got one!"

Johan felt the force from his fishing rod and immediately stood up excitedly, putting all his strength into it. The Ninetales tails that had been covering him scattered to the ground.

"Oowoo?"

Ninetales, lying beside him, cracked open its eyes slightly, then saw the familiar orange bouncing figure.

Plap plap plap—

An orange Magikarp was bouncing back and forth on the deck, its vacant eyes seeming to silently accuse Johan of catching it.

Johan: "..."

How many was this now?

"The seventh one, Rotom!"

Without Johan needing to count himself, Rotom, who had finished taking photos, told him the result.

Seven...

In just two hours, catching seven fish wasn't bad, but they were all Magikarp!

"I thank you, Rotom." Johan said ominously.

Rotom's body shook, trying to "remedy the situation," quickly saying:

"But—but! This Magikarp should be the highest level one, probably around level 40, Rotom!"

Plap plap plap—

The Magikarp continued performing its "Splash" attack.

"Level 40 and still not evolving..." Johan said through gritted teeth.

He irritably threw this "old fish" that could at most make fish head soup back into the sea.

If others didn't want it, he didn't want it either!

Level 40?

If you can grow to level 100 as a Magikarp, then I'll consider you impressive.

"Kalos region waters are also 'dominated' by Magikarp." Johan said dejectedly.

Plap plap plap—

The Magikarp that returned to the sea poked its head out of the water, looked at Johan, flicked its tail, splashing water.

Then swam away without looking back.

That attitude...

"Is it taunting me? Is it taunting me?" Johan looked at Ninetales.

"Oowoo..."

Ninetales gently exhaled white breath.

Calm down.

Crack crack crack—

Frost appeared on Johan's clothes, temples, and glasses.

Hiss—

He calmed down.

Johan sat back in his chair and picked up his fishing rod again.

Just now, he had almost told Regieleki and Rotom to electrify this entire sea area, but fortunately held back.

So fishing men were all about staying calm and unperturbed in the face of change.

"I don't believe I'll really get skunked."

Rolling up his sleeves, he skillfully baited the hook and cast again.

Actually, his fishing skills weren't bad now.

Too bad Magikarp were just too abundant.

"Even Kyogre can be caught, catching one fish that isn't Magikarp isn't too much to ask, right?"

Holding the fishing rod with one hand, he took out his phone with the other.

It showed the progress of the "Pokémon Hunter Base Raid Mission" jointly launched by the Kalos region International Police and League Police departments.

With Johan's "cheat-like" base intelligence gathering, many Pokémon Hunters active in the Kalos region had been arrested.

And the arrest speed and scale... could be said to be the first of its kind in Kalos region history.

In Johan's words...

"Gone completely wild."

Absolutely gone wild.

Now Pokémon Hunters in the eyes of International Police and League Police weren't just Pokémon Hunters anymore, but living, breathing achievements waiting to be "picked up."

When had catching Pokémon Hunters ever been this easy?

Pokémon Hunters were rampant for a reason.

On one hand, some Pokémon Hunters did have decent strength or backing.

But more importantly, Pokémon Hunters would dive deep into mountain forests where they couldn't be found.

Given the excellent natural environment of the Pokémon world, trying to find a Pokémon Hunter in vast forests was really no different from finding a needle in a haystack.

And with Johan providing intelligence, this most difficult part of catching Pokémon Hunters was essentially eliminated—wasn't that like picking up achievements?

Even the commotion from this raid operation attracted attention from the main League.

They highly praised Johan's actions and this operation.

As the initiator of this operation and the mission publisher... Johan calmly typed a few words in the group chat with one hand—

"Everyone's worked hard, when the mission is complete, I'll give everyone raises!"

As soon as this was said, the group erupted in cheers.

"Long live Teacher Johan!"

"Teacher Johan, through fire and water!"

"Teacher Johan, eternal god!"

"..."

Johan showed a satisfied smile.

No matter how much you talked or how big the promises, nothing was as real as a raise.

Anyway, the raises weren't coming from his pocket.

After the main League noticed this, Johan "petitioned for the people" to request raises for everyone.

And the achievements from this incident were enormous—a simple raise was certainly appropriate, so the main League naturally wouldn't refuse.

It's just that Johan earned half the credit.

But the League also got a relatively more stable Kalos region wilderness environment.

"Got a bite!" Johan felt the fishing rod shake again.

"Eighth one, Rotom."

Before the fish came up, Rotom had already quietly changed the number.

"Regi..."

Regieleki hung its head listlessly, completely deflated—its energy cubes were completely gone.

Gengar and Tinkaton's energy cubes had also taken considerable "losses," though they were better off than Regieleki.

And the biggest winner was undoubtedly Victini, who as the Victory Pokémon had similarly "gone wild" in today's "battle."

"Vii~"

Victini was very happy, then shared half of its energy cubes with Regieleki.

"Eleki?"

Seeing even more energy cubes than it had started with, Regieleki froze in place.

It scratched its head, somewhat crashing.

How were there more now?

Victini casually grabbed one and popped it in its mouth.

Although energy cubes weren't as good as macarons, they tasted great too.

"Vii~~"

Everyone having fun was what mattered, winning and losing wasn't the most important~

Victini gave the answer.

"Regi?"

Then Regieleki looked at Gengar and Tinkaton.

What about them...

"Ka-kaah~"

Gengar waved magnanimously, acting disdainful.

Just a few energy cubes—I have plenty.

"Cha~"

Tinkaton was equally generous.

As an "old-timer" in the "Old Johan Family," who didn't have a few hundred or thousand energy cubes "saved up"?

Besides...

Energy cubes could just be requested from Johan when they ran out, right?

Our "Old Johan Family" never lacked energy cubes.

"Eleki!"

A lightbulb appeared over Regieleki's head as it had an epiphany.

Right...

Just ask Johan when they ran out.

"Crunch crunch—"

Larvitar, who had been eating and watching the whole time, sighed and stood up, gently patting Regieleki's arm.

"Yoji~"

Young one, you still have much to learn~

"Regi!"

Regieleki nodded solemnly.

Kalos region, in the mountain forests behind Fula City.

Several figures moved somewhat frantically through the forest.

"Damn it, are the League guys crazy? We didn't get any advance warning, how did they suddenly launch a massive raid?"

"No advance warning was one thing, but the key is the League guys acted like they had radar, finding our base instantly. If we hadn't happened to be outside..."

"I heard it's not just us—lots of our colleagues' bases got raided!"

"I seriously suspect there's a traitor among us hunters, maybe more than one!"

Otherwise, the bases being directly raided made no sense.

But the problem was, even if there were "traitors," they couldn't know about so many Pokémon Hunter groups' bases.

"Speaking of which, where are we now?"

"Fula City."

"Fula City? Isn't that where they're holding some Wind Festival?"

"More people is better, right?"

"True..."

"Besides, I heard from some colleagues active around Fula City that they haven't been raided here—should be relatively safe."

"I remember there's supposed to be some powerful creature in the forests outside Fula City? Humans who enter the forest get attacked, lots of colleagues don't dare come."

"Hmph! Right now, what could be more dangerous than the League raids?"

"Makes sense..."

"And if we could catch that thing, all our losses... hehe..."

"Hehe hehe" ×N

Fula City, seaside port.

Whoosh—

Gentle sea breezes had been blowing almost continuously since approaching Fula City, carrying faint ocean scents and taking away some of summer's heat.

Wind was Fula City's characteristic and the "foundation" of its development.

Walking out of the port and looking up, windmills were everywhere as far as the eye could see—power-generating windmills.

Many surrounding towns' electricity came from Fula City.

But speaking of what was most eye-catching upon first arriving at Fula City, it was definitely a place like an amusement park on the sea outside the city.

It had ferris wheels, roller coasters, carousels and all sorts of facilities, with balloons of Pikachu, Eevee, Poké Balls, Lugia and various other shapes floating in the sky, looking festive.

That amusement park on the sea was exactly where Fula City held its Wind Festival activities and lit summer fireworks.

It was connected to the land and the entire Fula City by a winding road.

"They say Fula City's Wind Festival started from a promise with Lugia."

Valerie, who had also disembarked, said with a smile, wearing extremely tall wooden clogs and lace-trimmed black stockings, her wide sleeves fluttering in the wind like wings.

Valerie thought Johan didn't know about Fula City and the Wind Festival, so she continued:

"In the past, Fula City was a barren place, but people and Pokémon supported each other here, working hard to live. This bond moved Lugia, who promised to always bring wind to this land..."

And Fula City developed precisely because of this promise with Lugia and the continuous wind.

"That's the Sacred Flame."

Valerie pointed to a tall tower in Fula City's center, its top twinkling with crystalline light that shone like a star even in daylight.

Calling it "Sacred Flame" was really more like "starlight."

"They say Lugia uses the 'Sacred Flame' as a marker, sending wind here every year at fixed times."

Johan nodded.

Of course he knew all this, but he didn't interrupt Valerie, just thinking...

Did Lugia really know about this "promise"?

Or rather, the previous Lugia might have indeed kept this promise, but after the mountain fire fifty years ago, would Lugia still "honor" it?

After the Bell Tower incident in Ecruteak City in the Johto region, both Ho-Oh and Lugia had chosen to leave.

And the mountain fire incident in Fula City fifty years ago was definitely worse than the Bell Tower incident.

During the Bell Tower incident, humans just failed to save three Pokémon trapped in the burning tower, earning Ho-Oh and Lugia's anger.

In Fula City's mountain fire, there were hundreds, thousands, or even more Pokémon in the mountain forests.

"Maybe I can ask about it if there's a chance..."

"What?" Valerie didn't catch what he said.

Johan smiled and shook his head, "Nothing."

Valerie didn't press, just saying: "Teacher Johan, I'm going to prepare for the fashion design contest now, so..."

"No problem, go ahead, don't worry about me. I'll look around myself." Johan said.

"Alright." Valerie and the geishas behind her bowed slightly to him, "Then we'll take our leave first."

Getting on the contest's special vehicle, Valerie and the geishas left.

Johan stood by the seaside, looking at the endless ocean. Sunlight shone directly down, and the ripples stirred up by the sea breeze split the sunlight into pieces of scattered gold.

"Where should we go first..."

"Ka-kaah! Ka-kaah!"

Gengar pointed at the Wind Festival venue on the sea, shouting excitedly.

Let's go to the Pokémon Catch Race!

Johan remembered that in the movie "The Power of Us," when Ash participated in the Pokémon Catch Race, he provided several extremely memorable famous scenes.

First was riding a rampaging Tyranitar barehanded, second was casually helping up a fallen Tyranitar...

That was the Desert Tyrant Tyranitar, not the baby Larvitar.

Super rookie protagonist powers displayed to perfection.

But...

"The Wind Festival hasn't started yet, and the Pokémon Catch Race hasn't started either." Johan said.

Speaking of which, he was really curious what kind of Pokémon Fula City, as the host, would provide for trainers to catch in this "Pokémon Catch Race."

Would there be pseudo-legendaries?

If there were pseudo-legendaries... would it be Tyranitar?

If Larvitar saw Tyranitar... that would definitely be fun, right?

Imagining that scene, Johan's lips unconsciously curved upward.

"Ka-kaah..."

Hearing that the Pokémon contest hadn't started yet, Gengar's ears drooped.

"Come on." Johan patted the little fatty's back, "I heard Fula City's ice cream is also famous, how about..."

"Ka-kaah!"

Gengar suddenly raised its head, holding up one hand with three fingers, then feeling that wasn't enough, raised the other hand too.

I want three! No! Six!

Johan couldn't help but laugh.

"Alright, alright, just don't get a stomachache."

Gengar put its hands on its hips and raised its head.

Me get a stomachache?

Ridiculous!

The Zygarde core on Johan's shoulder half-raised its head.

[What is ice cream?]

Johan smiled mysteriously, "I'll let you try some later."

In the mountain forest.

"There!"

A golden figure, accompanied by blue lightning, moved through the forest at extremely high speed.

Behind it, several Pokémon Hunters in mountain gear followed closely.

"Weavile, Ice Beam!"

Bang—!!

An ice flower bloomed on a tree.

"Damn it!"

"Let's see how long you can run! Houndoom, lock onto its scent, don't let it escape! This is an unseen rare Pokémon! It actually delivered itself to our door!"

They had just been resting when they suddenly came under attack from this mysterious Pokémon.

But fortunately, they still had some skill.

After all, being able to escape the League's raids, they couldn't do it without some ability.

Although they were still injured by that guy, hurting quite a few Pokémon, they had also injured that guy.

Mysterious, rare, and powerful—these factors combined meant this guy could definitely sell for an incredible price.

With their bases raided and heavy losses, they could use this guy to recoup.

"This guy's really fast!"

"Hmph! As long as it's still on land, it can't escape!"

Houndoom's keen sense of smell was his confidence.

But before long, his confidence disappeared.

Because they chased to a cliff three or four meters high with a fast-flowing stream below, and Houndoom stopped at the cliff.

"Jumped in the river?"

"Chase downstream, it can't go far!"

They followed the stream's direction downstream.

But upstream from the stream.

A pink-haired girl was playing with a Teddiursa and Ditto by the stream.

"Come on, Teddiursa, it's okay, just taking a bath, don't move around."

"Teddi!"

Teddiursa struggled but didn't dare use force, afraid of hurting the girl.

It suddenly pointed toward the stream.

"Teddi!"

"What's wrong?" The girl Risa looked over puzzledly.

Splash—

Suddenly.

The water surface broke, and a golden, bedraggled figure leaped out from the water, crashing onto the rocks not far from Risa.

"This is... injured?" Risa was startled and quickly stood up.

"Teddiursa, Ditto, come help!"

Bang!!

But before they could get close, a blue lightning bolt exploded in front of Risa.

The yellow figure struggled to open its eyes, glaring fiercely.

"Zeraaa!"

A book written by a friend.

"Pokémon World's Breeding Master"

"Groudon wants to learn flying from me? Really?"

——

Beckett transmigrated to the Pokémon world and obtained a breeding simplification panel.

Learning Roar = Roar loudly 200 times, learning Rest = Take a nap

"Garchomp, want to learn Dragon Dance?"

"What, you want Roserade to learn Quiver Dance?"

"My Gallade is fair-skinned, beautiful, and long-legged—learning Thunder Kick is very reasonable, right?"

As Beckett's reputation spread wider and wider, it seemed an incredible existence came knocking.

"You say you want to learn to fly? Real flying?"

Beckett looked seriously at the non-flying one in front of him.

[Pokémon: Groudon]

[Breeding Goal: Learn to fly, real flying]

[Breeding Requirements: ...]
